what_happened: Job 20261030-185437-1tbs ("Reclaim interrupted jobs' build dirs; gate disk before the producer") failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic judged the reclaim design sound, and the code the plan cites exists. One major finding remained. The plan's drain tests would include tests/common/mod.rs with a #[path] attribute inside the athena-cli library's unit tests. That module calls athena_cli::wiring::capabilities(), a crate cannot name itself that way, and lib.rs has no `extern crate self as athena_cli`. So the tests for criteria 1, 2 and 3(b) would not compile. There was one minor finding. Criterion 2's test passes on today's code, and the new pre-producer check is left to a user answer that may not arrive before the producer runs. There was one nit: nobody checked whether Records::load accepts a single committed Job stub with no Reading. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Planning checks that the seams a plan names exist, but it does not require the plan to show that a test fixture can be compiled where it is placed. Here a shared test module was pulled into a library's unit tests, and it refers to the crate by an external name that the crate cannot use from inside. Only the critic reading the code finds this, and only late. Planning has three fixed rounds and keeps no partial plan, so a build problem found in round 3 loses all the planning spend. No cheap mechanical check, such as compiling a stub of the planned test file, exists. Open questions that reading the code would settle (the Records::load stub, the producer.rs scope) are also left in the plan.
prevention: Add a planning check that runs before the critic. For each planned test file, it resolves where the test lives (crate, module path, #[path] includes) and verifies that every path the included code names (such as athena_cli::...) is reachable from that crate. A cheap compile check of a stub test file in the target location would do. A plan that puts a test where its fixture cannot build should be sent back for repair in an early round. The check should also require that the plan settle code-answerable open questions, such as stub loading and scope, by reading the code.
proposed_request: Reclaim the build directories (target/) of interrupted jobs, and gate free disk before the producer starts. A job is interrupted when its records show it as dispatched, it has no registry entry, and its job lock is free. Take the lock while removing the directory. Skip the drain's own jobs. Keep work trees and candidates. Run the reclaim at drain start and before each run. If free disk is still below the threshold before the producer, hold the job as the dispatch gate already does, and say so in the job's status. Acceptance: (1) with an interrupted job's target/ present, drain start removes it and keeps the work tree; (2) a job that is not interrupted, or whose lock is held, keeps its target/; (3) low disk before the producer holds the job and does not run the producer. Put the tests where the fixture builds: either in crates/athena-cli/tests as an integration test, or in a unit test that does not include tests/common/mod.rs. Before planning, check that the chosen test location can import athena_cli::wiring::capabilities. Allowed files: crates/athena-cli/src/run/ (drain, disk, producer gating as needed), their tests, and the changelog entry. Settle by reading the code whether Records::load accepts a single committed Job stub with no Reading, and whether the producer.rs change is needed. Do not ask the user.
